transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, I really don't want to waste your time. But... well, I guess I'm mostly here because my sleep has sort of... fallen apart recently? 

I mean, I know everyone gets busy, and I really want to do a good job at work—I'm a management analyst—and with my extra classes, so it's probably just me trying too hard to stay on top of things. But I'll close my laptop for the night and just lie in bed in my apartment for hours, still mentally rechecking all my work deadlines, and worrying about tuition payments, and going over class assignments. I just want to make sure I haven't dropped the ball on anything, you know? Is that... does that make sense? 

It's just getting a bit exhausting because even when I do finally manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off. I'm sorry, I hope I'm explaining this right.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with sleep, and has it been happening even when you didn’t have work or school stress on your mind?

Um, well, I guess it's been... maybe about a year and three months now? I hope it's okay that I waited this long to come in, I really thought I could just push through it. It started right around the time I began my evening graduate certificate program, um, while keeping my full-time analyst job. I just really want to excel at both, so I know I took on a lot. 

As for when I don't have work or school on my mind... honestly, since I started the program, there hasn't really been a single day where I wasn't thinking about one or the other. I'm just trying to be responsible and make sure I don't let anyone down at the office or in my cohort. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Do you find that your worrying happens more often than not, even when there isn’t an immediate deadline or problem to solve?

Um, yeah, I guess it does happen a lot. I mean, I really try not to let it get out of hand, because I know I should just be grateful for the opportunities I have, but... yeah, even when there isn't a huge deadline right in front of me, my mind just sort of... keeps going? 

It's like it just jumps around. Like, I'll be thinking about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then suddenly I'm worrying about whether I'm just wasting money on this certificate program, and then... well, I worry a lot about whether my family thinks I'm in over my head and can't handle things. I just really want them to be proud of me, you know? 

So I guess I do end up treating every little thing like it's... like it could completely derail my whole future if I don't handle it perfectly. I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, and I'm really trying to be better about it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not overcomplicating it.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there’s no clear reason or specific problem to focus on, like when you're alone or trying to relax?

Um, I guess... well, I don't really have a lot of time to just relax, honestly. I'm usually trying to stay productive, so I'm not just sitting around doing nothing. But, um, I suppose if I am just by myself, like on a Sunday afternoon when I've actually caught up on everything... my mind doesn't really stay quiet. 

I wouldn't say I'm worrying for absolutely no reason, because there's always *something* to prepare for, right? But I guess I do find myself kind of... scanning? Like, trying to figure out what I might have forgotten to worry about. I just want to make sure I'm not missing anything important. I'm really trying to get better at just enjoying my downtime, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.

Do you find that your worrying is persistent and occurs even when there’s no specific problem or stressor to focus on, rather than being limited to times when you’re facing a particular challenge at work or school?

Um, I'm sorry, I feel like I might be frustrating you by not giving a very clear answer, and I really do want to be helpful here. But... I'm not entirely sure? 

I don't think I really experience it when there's absolutely zero stressor or no problem at all. It feels like there's always at least a little something I'm facing, even if it's just a minor email I need to send for my analyst job or a small reading for my program. So I haven't really noticed myself just... worrying about completely nothing. It always feels tied to a real challenge, even a small one, if that makes sense? 

I always try to keep my focus on things I can actually work on and fix. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you, I promise I'm not trying to be difficult.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like feeling restless, being easily fatigued, or having muscle tension, even when you're not actively working or studying?

Um, physical symptoms... well, I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or, you know, being lazy. I always try to push through because I know my team relies on me as an analyst, and I want to do a good job. But, um... I guess I do get pretty tired? Like, easily fatigued, like you mentioned. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but by midafternoon at the office, I just feel completely drained. It gets to the point where even just doing the little things, like answering normal emails or... or just walking to the subway at the end of the day, it takes so much effort. I keep thinking I just need a good weekend to catch up, but even when I try to rest on Saturday and Sunday, it doesn't really seem to give me my energy back. 

I'm really trying to manage my stamina better, I promise. I know I probably just need to build up better habits and drink more water or something. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable, easily annoyed, or emotionally reactive lately, even in situations where you wouldn’t normally expect to feel that way?

Um, irritable? I... I don't think so. I mean, I really try hard to be a positive person, especially at work. I know how important it is to be a good team player, so I always try to keep a smile on and be helpful, even when things get stressful. 

I don't think I've been snapping at anyone or getting easily annoyed. I'd feel terrible if I made someone else's day harder just because I was feeling a little stressed. I guess sometimes I might feel a tiny bit frustrated if I'm really behind on a project, but I always keep it to myself. I definitely wouldn't say I'm emotionally reactive or anything like that. I really try to keep things professional and pleasant. I hope that's okay? I'm not trying to hide anything, I just really try to be mindful of how I treat people.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, even when you’re not particularly tired or distracted?

Um, concentrating... I, well, I really hate to admit this because I pride myself on being very thorough and detail-oriented at work. But, um, lately I guess I have been having a little bit of trouble with it? 

I don't want it to sound like I'm slacking off, because I'm really trying my best. But sometimes I'll be sitting at my desk, looking at a financial model, or even just doing a reading for my program, and... and I'll realize I've just been staring at it for ages. Like, I'll read the exact same paragraph maybe five times, and I just can't seem to absorb what it says. 

It's not that the work is too hard, I promise. It's just that my brain... it kind of runs away from me? Like, I'll be trying to focus, but my head is already off running through everything else that could possibly go wrong with the project, or what I need to do next. I always try to catch myself and refocus, though! I'm really working on being more present. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm completely incompetent at my job.
Do you ever find yourself becoming anxious or worried specifically about not being able to fall asleep, like a fear that sleep won’t come no matter what you do?

Um, anxious specifically about not sleeping... I, well, I don't think so? I really hope I'm answering this right, I don't want to give you bad information. 

But no, I don't think I have a fear of sleep not coming, exactly. I mean, like I mentioned, my brain is usually just so busy running through all my work tasks and making sure I didn't let my team down that day... but I'm not really focused on the sleep part itself. I usually just lie there thinking about my projects and how to do better tomorrow. 

Is that... is it okay if I don't have that specific worry? I just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for your assessment. I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking!
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried about things on more days than not, even if just a little bit, over the past six months or longer?

Um, more days than not? I, well... I guess maybe I do worry a bit most days? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm totally falling apart, because I really do try to keep it together. 

But, um, if I'm being completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture—it feels like my mind is just always going. Like, it just keeps jumping from one thing to the next. I'll be worrying about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then suddenly I'm stressing about whether I'm just wasting money on my degree program, and then I start worrying that my family is going to think I can't handle my life... 

It's like I treat every single small issue like it could completely derail my whole future. I know it probably sounds silly, and I really try to remind myself that things are fine, but... it's just hard to turn it off. I guess it has been like that for a while now, definitely more than six months. I really hope I'm not overreacting by saying that. Is it normal to feel that way sometimes?
Do you find it difficult to control your worrying, even when you try to calm your mind or focus on something else?

Um, controlling the worry... I, well, I really try my hardest to. I know I should be able to just snap out of it, and I don't want you to think I'm not putting the effort in to calm down. I really do try to tell myself to just stop and focus on one thing at a time. 

But... I guess sometimes it gets a little away from me? Like, I'll try to push a thought away, but then that one worry just immediately leads to another one. And before I know it, instead of actually getting my work done, I'm just sitting there checking my calendar, and then my budget, and then my class assignments... over and over again. 

I know I shouldn't let it spiral like that, and I'm really trying to get better at catching it early. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely out of control... I mean, I do manage to get things done eventually! Am I explaining that in a way that helps? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find that your worries often jump from one topic to another, and that it’s hard to stop worrying once you start, even when you try to focus on something else?

Um, yeah, I think that's exactly it... I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself from just a minute ago, I hope I'm not rambling too much! But yes, they definitely jump around a lot. 

Like I was saying, I really do try to just tell myself, "Okay, stop, just focus on this one report," but it's like my brain won't listen. One worry about work just instantly turns into a worry about my classes, and then my finances... and then I'm just cycling through my calendar, and my budget spreadsheet, and my syllabus, just over and over. And I realize I haven't actually accomplished anything, which just makes me feel worse. 

I know I should be better at just shutting it down once it starts. I really am trying to work on that. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering what you're looking for!
Has your worrying ever made it hard for you to function normally, like affecting your job performance, relationships, or ability to do everyday things?

Um, well... I really try not to let it get in the way of things. I want to be someone who can handle it all, you know? But, um, if I'm being totally honest—and I know I should be honest with you—it has been getting a little difficult lately. 

I don't want to sound like I'm completely dropping the ball, but I have, um, missed a couple of work deadlines recently. And I'm falling a bit behind in my certificate classes, which I feel terrible about because I really do care about my career. 

And, um, I used to be really good about keeping up with things that made me feel grounded, like going for runs, or doing yoga, and even just cooking nice meals for myself. But lately, I just... I haven't been doing those things as much. I guess I just get so wrapped up in everything else. 

I know I need to get back on track, and I promise I'm really going to try harder to stay on top of things. I hope that doesn't make me sound too irresponsible? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit.
Do you find that your worries are not limited to specific situations, but instead happen across many areas of your life, like work, school, relationships, and other everyday things?

Um, yes, I... I guess they do cover a lot of different areas. I really wish they didn't, and I know I should be able to just keep things compartmentalized. I don't want you to think I'm just complaining about everything in my life! 

But, um, it's just that my mind keeps jumping around so much. Like, I'll be worrying if I'm falling behind on my analysis projects at work, and then suddenly I'm worrying if I'm just completely wasting my money on my certificate classes... and then I start stressing about whether my family is going to think I just can't handle being an adult. 

It's silly, I know it is. But it's like I treat every single tiny issue like it's going to completely derail my entire future. I know I shouldn't blow things out of proportion like that, and I'm really trying to be more rational about it all. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm totally incapable of handling normal life stuff!

Do you find that your worrying is not limited to specific stressors but instead tends to jump across many different areas of your life, like work, school, relationships, and even small everyday things?

Oh, um, I'm so sorry, did I not explain that very well just a second ago? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need! 

But yes, it really does jump around just like you're describing. Like I was just saying, my mind just keeps bouncing from worrying if I'm falling behind at work, to stressing over whether I'm wasting my money on school... and then I start panicking that my family will think I just can't handle things. I know it sounds a bit dramatic, and I really am trying to be better at keeping things in perspective, but I just end up treating every little small issue like it could completely derail my whole future.

Um... no, not really. I don't think I walk around feeling tense for absolutely no reason. I mean, I always try to have a reason if I'm feeling stressed, you know? Like, I'm a management analyst, so my job is all about finding the logic in things, and I really try to apply that to myself, too. 

I don't just sit around waiting for the sky to fall or anything like that. I really try to stay positive! If I'm feeling anxious, it's usually tied to something specific, like the work deadlines or the classes I mentioned earlier. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm completely irrational or just making up things to be scared of. I really do try to keep a good head on my shoulders about it all.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried about things on more days than not, even if just a little bit, over the past six months or longer?

Um, yes, I... I guess I would have to say it's been most days. I really hate admitting that, because I feel like I should have gotten a handle on it by now. I don't want you to think I'm just weak or not trying hard enough to manage my stress! 

But, um, it's been going on for a while... maybe about a year and three months? It really started when I decided to take on the evening graduate certificate program while still working my full-time analyst job. I thought I could juggle it all perfectly, you know? I really wanted to prove I could handle the extra workload. But ever since then, the worrying has just been... well, pretty constant. 

I know I probably took on too much, and I'm really trying to work on my time management so I don't feel this way. Is it normal to feel this overwhelmed when you add that much to your plate? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be.
Do you find that your worries are often not limited to specific situations, but instead occur across many areas of your life, such as work, school, relationships, and even small everyday things?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I think you might have just asked me that a few minutes ago? Did I not explain it clearly enough the first time? I can totally try to give a better answer if you need me to! 

But yeah, like I mentioned before, it really does bounce around between my job, my certificate program, and worrying about what my family thinks of me. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or repeat myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for. Did you need me to go into more detail about one of those specific areas, or did I maybe misunderstand the question earlier? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you often feel a sense of dread or impending doom, like something terrible is going to happen, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Um, no, I don't think I get that. Like a sense of doom? No, definitely not. I really try to keep a positive outlook, you know? 

Like I was saying before, I try to keep my worries tied to logical things, like my projects at work or my classes. I don't just... sit around feeling like a disaster is going to strike out of thin air. That sounds really scary, and I'm so glad I don't have that! 

I hope that's an okay answer? I mean, I hope I'm answering these questions the right way for you. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you exactly what you need to know to figure all this out.
Do you ever feel anxious or start worrying when things in your life are actually going smoothly and there’s no clear reason to be stressed?

Um, well... I guess I try really hard to just enjoy it when things are going well. I mean, I don't want to be the kind of person who ruins a good moment by overthinking it, you know? 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, which I want to be for you... sometimes, even when I'm caught up on my analyst reports and my classes are fine, I still feel this sort of... hum of worry in the background? Like I should be doing something, or I forgot something important. I try to push it down because I know it's silly to stress when there's no fire to put out. I really hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for the good days. Is it common to still feel a little on edge even when things are okay? I just want to make sure I'm not totally overreacting.
